# Golden fit set

The NONMEM anchors pin specific features and the Tier-3 tests pin convergence
bands, but neither tracks **the same reference models across releases**. A small
drift in θ, SE or OFV from an unrelated change would otherwise be noticed by a
user, by a downstream repository, or by chance. The golden fit set closes that
gap (#2635). It sits beside the anchors and does not replace any of them.

| | |
|---|---|
| Models | `tools/golden-fits/models.tsv`: one row per estimator, structural or endpoint family, each an existing `examples/` model |
| Runner | `tools/golden-fits/golden.py` (`run`, `report`, `bands`), standard-library Python only |
| Workflow | `.github/workflows/golden-fits.yml`, nightly 04:30 UTC and on dispatch, **Linux only** |
| Output | the job summary table, and a `golden-fits-results` artifact kept 90 days |
| Guard | `tests/golden_fit_set.rs` (per PR, runs no fit) |

## What a nightly does

1. Fits every model with the **last release's** binary on the release's own
   `examples/` and `data/`, then caches the result under the tag. That fit runs
   once per release. On every other night the cache supplies it.
2. Builds `ferx` at the head of `main` and fits the same models.
3. Downloads the previous scheduled run's results, if one is available.
4. Writes the table to the job summary.

Each row records OFV, every θ, ω (including off-diagonals of a block), κ and σ
with its SE, the iteration count, the convergence flag and the covariance status.
The columns show the change against the release: ΔOFV as an absolute value, the
largest relative change (`|head − release| / |release|`) over the estimates
and over the SEs together with the parameter it occurs on, and the change in iterations. A `Δ OFV prev` column
compares against the previous nightly, which ties a change to one day's merges.
For every model that changed, a collapsible block lists each parameter that
moved.

A `NaN` anywhere counts as a change, even when the release had `NaN` in the
same place. The report never folds a `NaN` away the
way `max` would (see AGENTS.md on `f64::max`). A row whose model or data file
differs from the release's copy is marked as such, so an edited example does not
read as engine drift. All fits run single-threaded (`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`).

Fit numbers come from **Linux** only. See
[Reference platform](sdlc.qmd#reference-platform-linux). Do not compare a macOS
run of `golden.py` with the nightly table.

## Report-only, then fail-on-band

The job is **report-only until 2026-12-07**, the date in `FAIL_ON_BAND_FROM` in
`golden.py`. That gives about 30 nightlies, starting 2026-11-05, to measure the
natural spread of each model. Two things happen on that date:

- If `tools/golden-fits/bands.json` has not been committed, the job **fails**,
  and the failure names the missing file. A report with no end date gets read for
  a week and is then ignored, so the date is enforced and does not expire
  quietly.
- Once `bands.json` is committed, the job fails when any quantity moves outside
  its band relative to the release, when a fit that succeeded at the release fails
  at head, or when a model or parameter has no measured band.

`tests/golden_fit_set.rs` requires this page and `golden.py` to give the same
date. To move the date, change both in the same commit.

### Measuring the bands

```bash
# the last 30 scheduled runs' results, one directory each
for id in $(gh run list --workflow golden-fits.yml --branch main --event schedule \
              --status success --limit 30 --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId'); do
  gh run download "$id" --name golden-fits-results --dir "hist/$id"
done
python3 tools/golden-fits/golden.py bands hist/*/head.json   # writes tools/golden-fits/bands.json
```

A band is `headroom × max |x − median|` over the nightlies, with a default
headroom of 2. It is relative for estimates and SEs and absolute for OFV and
iterations. If the spread of a quantity is exactly zero, the band falls back to
a floor (1e-6 relative, 1e-3 OFV, 2 iterations), because a band of 0 would fail
on the last bit. The floors are a choice, not a measurement, and `bands.json`
records them. `bands` refuses to run on fewer than 30 nightlies. A quantity
that went `NaN` during the window gets a `NaN` band. The report treats a
non-finite band as missing, so the quantity fails until the bands are
re-measured.

### An intentional change

When a pull request moves a golden model on purpose (a new default, or a fixed
likelihood), dispatch the workflow on the branch, download its
`golden-fits-results` artifact, and pin the model's new state together with the
reason and the PR:

```bash
python3 tools/golden-fits/golden.py accept warfarin_saem --head head.json \
  --reason "#1234: SAEM burn-in default 150 → 200"
```

This writes an entry under `accepted` in `bands.json` that holds the model's
OFV, iterations, estimates and SEs at that point. The model is **not exempted**.
From then on it is banded against the accepted state instead of the release. The
row still shows its change against the release, marked `✔︎`, but a later,
unrelated drift away from the accepted state fails the job as usual (`🔺`). An
entry without a pinned state also fails the job.

At each release the baseline absorbs the change, so clear `accepted` then. The
`accepted` entries for a release are also its list of "estimates changed for
model X" lines for the release notes.

## Seeing a change before it merges

Dispatch the workflow on a branch:

```bash
gh workflow run golden-fits.yml --ref <branch>            # all models
gh workflow run golden-fits.yml --ref <branch> -f only=warfarin,warfarin_saem
```

A perturbation, for example a changed default, appears as `≠` on every model it
reaches, with the parameters that moved listed under *Changed models*. The guard
test checks this on synthetic results: a 1% change on one θ must be reported on
that θ, and the unperturbed twin must report `=`.

## Adding or retiring a model

- Add a row to `models.tsv`. Its `family` must differ from every other row's;
  the guard checks this, along with the existence of the model and data files.
- Never reuse an `id` for a different model. Retire the old id and add a new
  one, so each history stays with its own model.
- A new model has no release value until the next release. Its row shows `🆕`.
  Once fail-on-band mode is active, a new model also needs a band, so re-measure
  `bands.json` after the model has run for 30 nightlies.
- GN, GN-hybrid, Laplace, AGQ, Bayes and VI are not covered yet because no
  `examples/` model uses them. Add a row when one does, instead of writing a
  model file just for this set.
